headline: Chinese makers supplied more than 97 percent of the roughly 19,100 humanoid robots shipped worldwide in the first half of 2026, Startup Fortune reports, while Tesla's Optimus fell far short of its 2025 target.
score_reason: Useful market picture but the underlying data sources are not named and the outlet mixes opinion with figures.
importance_line: Companies and governments weighing humanoid robots would mostly be buying Chinese-made machines today, but the figures are secondhand and the robots still work well below human productivity.
summary: Startup Fortune reports, citing unnamed industry data, that about 19,100 humanoid robots shipped worldwide in the first half of 2026, more than triple a year earlier, with Chinese makers such as AgiBot, Unitree and UBTech supplying over 97 percent while Tesla's Optimus built only a few hundred against a 5,000 target for 2025. The article also notes that robots deployed at BYD and Foxconn reach only 30 to 50 percent of human productivity and that China's planning agency has warned of overheating.
notes: Opinionated aggregator piece; primary data not identified.
